st: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft, adding a splash of water if it sticks.
Add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt. Cook for 5 minutes until they break down into a sauce.
Stir in the greens and [[0.5 cup]] of the water. Cover and cook for 10 minutes until tender, then season with salt and set aside warm.
Bring [[3 cups]] of the water to a boil in a heavy pot.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] of the cornmeal with the remaining [[1 cup]] water in a bowl until smooth. Whisk it into the boiling water.
Cook the thin porridge on medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring often, until it thickens and bubbles.
Turn the heat to low. Add the remaining cornmeal a handful at a time, stirring hard with a wooden spoon after each addition so no lumps form.
Keep pressing and turning the mixture against the side of the pot for 8 minutes until it is very thick and pulls away from the pot.
Cover and let it steam on the lowest heat for 5 minutes.
Scoop the nsima into wet bowls or shape into smooth balls. Serve warm with the greens and tomato relish, eating it with your hands.
Pat the fish dry. Cut three shallow slashes into each side so the seasoning can get in.
Rub the fish with the juice of half the lemon, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Let it sit for 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the fish for 6 minutes per side until the skin is golden and the flesh flakes easily at the thickest part. Move to a plate.
In the same pan, cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt. Cook for 8 minutes until thick and saucy.
Spoon the tomato sauce over or beside the fish and top with the lemon slices. Serve with nsima or rice.
Wash the leaves well and chop them into thin strips. If using pumpkin leaves, strip off tough stems and fibers first.
Grind the peanuts in a blender or food processor into a coarse flour. Be careful not to turn it into butter.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and [[0.75 tsp]] salt. Cook for 5 minutes until they soften.
Add the greens and [[1 cup]] water. Cover and cook for 10 minutes until wilted and tender.
Sprinkle in the ground peanuts and stir well. Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes until thick.
Taste, add salt if needed, and serve hot beside nsima.

ing: or dried anchovies or small dried fish
st: Rinse the dried fish under cool water and soak in a bowl of warm water for 10 minutes. Drain and squeeze dry.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the fish for 3 minutes until slightly crisp, then move to a plate.
In the same oil, cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes until they break down.
Return the fish to the pan with [[1 cup]] water. Cover and simmer on low for 10 minutes.
Taste before salting since the fish is already salty. Serve hot with nsima.
Warm the milk until just lukewarm, not hot. Stir in the yeast and [[1 tbsp]] of the sugar and wait 5 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl, mix the flour, the rest of the sugar, the salt and the cardamom if using.
Add the egg and the foamy milk. Stir to a soft, sticky dough.
Knead on a floured counter for 6 minutes until smooth and springy.
Cover the bowl with a towel and let the dough rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Roll the dough about 1/2 inch thick and cut into triangles or squares.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C). Test with a small piece of dough, which should bubble right away.
Fry a few at a time for 2 minutes per side until puffed and deep golden brown.
Drain on paper towels. Serve warm, plain or with tea.
Put the sweet potato and pumpkin cubes in a pot with [[3 cups]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and cook for 20 minutes until very soft.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a small pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes until golden.
Drain the cooked vegetables, saving a little of the cooking water.
Mash them in the pot until mostly smooth.
Stir in the ground peanuts and the cooked onion. Add a splash of the reserved water if too thick.
Season with the remaining salt and cook on low for 5 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy. Serve warm.
In a bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry one and stir until just combined. A few small lumps are fine.
Let the batter rest for 10 minutes so the baking powder gets going.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a non-stick skillet over medium-low heat.
Pour in about [[0.25 cup]] batter per cake. Cook for 3 minutes until bubbles appear and the edges set.
Flip and cook for 2 more minutes until golden and cooked through.
Repeat with the remaining oil and batter. Serve warm.
